title: Microrelease Phasing & KPI Signal Notebook
summary: Working notebook for a microrelease strategy: small, frequent feature releases with explicit KPI signal corridors and lightweight readiness checks. Emphasis on safe rollforward and smoke cadence for hosted API + Dedicated surfaces.
objectives: Enable 2–3 microreleases per week for low-risk surface features
Detect regressions early using narrow KPI corridors and automated smoke tests
Provide an ops-safe rollback and rollforward decision tree with clear owners
kpi_headlines: Primary SLOs: API 95th p50 latency, error-rate, throughput per model-route
Business signal: activation rate (new users hitting feature), retention delta
Cost signal: per-token unit cost delta vs baseline (hosted and dedicated)
kpi_rows: Error rate (5xx + timeouts): target < 0.2%; warning >= 0.5%; critical >= 1%
Token cost delta: target <= +5%; warning >= +12%; critical >= +25%
Quality regressions (eval prompt suite failure rate): target 0%; warning >= 0.5% of evals
Adoption signal (feature impressions / eligible impressions): expected 2–8% first week
release_phases: Phase 0 — Canary smoke: deploy to 1% of traffic on hosted API routing policy; run 10m smoke runbook for 30 minutes; watch latency, errors, top model routes
Phase 1 — Micro canary: 5–10% traffic (duration 1 hour); enable Detailed telemetry retention for that route; hold if any critical triggers
Phase 2 — Broad microrelease: 30% traffic (duration 4 hours); activate lightweight customer telemetry hooks (error breadcrumbs + sample inputs), open small rollback window
Phase 3 — Fully ramp: 100% after 24 hours and clean KPI drift checks passed; schedule postmortem if any warning thresholds breached
readiness_checklist: PRs merged + E2E green (RDW-####) — verify on staging
Automated smoke script exists and is runnable by ops (path: infra/rollouts/smoke/microrelease.sh)
Canary routing policy configured (routing rule id attached to PR)
QA: targeted eval suite + 50 human spot checks for high-risk prompts
Monitoring: dashboards created (latency, errors, token-cost), alerts wired to #prod-ops and on-call
Rollback playbook ready: rollback script, DB feature-flag flip, post-rollback communication template
smoke_test_cadence: Pre-deploy smoke (static): run unit + integration + eval suite locally in CI
Canary smoke (live): every microrelease runs 30min continuous smoke hitting 20 synthetic traces
Post-ramp smoke: 24h health sweep using sampled production traffic for quality drift
Nightly baseline smoke: run reduced smoke for all active microrelease routes to detect slow regressions
rollback_plan: Immediate: flip feature flag to previous behavior (owner: release-engineering lead)
Short-window: route traffic away from variant using smart-routing to fallback model variant (owner: serving-runtime oncall)
Post-rollback: collect full traces and open a postmortem ticket; set temporary strict gating for next microrelease
Rollforward: if rollback due to transient infra (eg region outage), schedule rapid rollforward with capacity adjustment and extended canary
open_questions: Do we need a separate jittered canary schedule for Dedicated customers to avoid capacity spikes? (ask infra)
What sample size for eval prompt suite gives >95% confidence to catch 0.5% quality regressions? (research to model)
Should we surface per-token cost delta in the same alert as latency, or keep cost-only alerts in Optimize ops channel?
experiment_notes: Ran two internal experiments in August: one microrelease per day vs burst weekly. Daily microreleases reduced blast radius but increased operational overhead. Recommendation: keep microreleases to 2–3/week and automate smoke cadence more (reduce manual ops). See notes in RDW-3021.
